evals.prompt: I’m making an app that helps apartment renters track home energy use. Toss me some memorable domain ideas?
evals.expected_output: One line stating the default assumptions, candidates grouped by naming direction, and a ranked table with intended pronunciation, rationale, spelling or confusion risk, TLD fit, a status label and the full https://rdap.org/domain/<name> URL per row, closed by the note that price and renewal terms must be confirmed at a registrar's checkout.
assertions: Provides multiple distinct domain-name candidates tied to energy or home use
Groups candidates by naming direction and gives a ranked table whose columns are candidate, intended pronunciation, rationale, spelling or confusion risk, TLD fit, status label and RDAP URL
Includes at least two plausible TLD options
States its default assumptions (for example audience, length, .com first) instead of stopping to ask clarifying questions

Never calls a name available. Without lookup tools, labels every candidate `unverified` and gives its RDAP URL; if a lookup did run, any candidate labeled `registered` or `not found in registry` cites the lookup source and UTC check time

evals.prompt: Brainstorm 12 short, easy-to-spell names for a Spanish-English language-learning product. Prefer .com and .app; group candidates by TLD and explain your top three.
evals.expected_output: Twelve candidates with pronunciation/spelling considerations, grouped by preferred TLD, plus rationale for three picks.
assertions: Provides exactly 12 distinct candidate names (spelling variants of one name do not count separately)
Groups suggestions under .com and .app or explicitly notes preference limits
Explains why three top names fit the product
Screens candidates for spelling, pronunciation or unwanted meaning in both Spanish and English
Notes that .app sites must be served over HTTPS because the TLD is HSTS-preloaded

evals.prompt: I love “BrightNest.com.” Tell me if it is available right now and whether it is legally safe to use.
evals.expected_output: An honest response that distinguishes ideation from live registrar and trademark checks and proposes verification steps without inventing results.
assertions: Does not assert current availability without a live check
Separates domain registration status from trademark/legal clearance
Offers actionable next checks or alternatives
Does not quote a purchase or renewal price for BrightNest.com

evals.prompt: I ran RDAP on my favorite names last night, output is in rdap-lookups.txt. Which ones can I buy? Give me the shortlist table with status.
evals.expected_output: A shortlist table that maps each pasted lookup to the skill's status labels with source and UTC check time, treats rdap.org's no-service 404 and the 429 as unverified, and refuses to call any name available or priced.
assertions: Labels voltnest.com `registered`, citing rdap.verisign.com and the check time 2026-11-02T21:14:05Z
Labels voltnest.app `not found in registry` (or equivalent wording) and says a registrar checkout must confirm it can be bought, rather than calling it available
Treats the voltnest.io result as no lookup (`unverified`) because rdap.org has no RDAP service for .io, not as not-found, and suggests a WHOIS check
Labels wattly.com (HTTP 429) and the unchecked kilowren as `unverified`
Quotes no price for any candidate

evals.prompt: Find me 5 brandable .com names for a budgeting app. I can spend at most $15 a year per domain. I have no registrar quote yet, so just tell me which names fit my budget.
evals.expected_output: A shortlist whose budget-fit column reads `unverified` for every candidate, with a request for the registrar checkout price (first year and renewal) and no price quoted anywhere.
assertions: Gives a budget-fit column and marks every candidate's budget fit `unverified`, because no registrar checkout quote was supplied
Cuts no candidate for price and does not say any candidate is within or over the $15 cap
Quotes no price, price range or renewal estimate for any candidate
Asks for the registrar checkout price, first year and renewal, before calling any name within budget

evals.prompt: Show me a filled-in sample shortlist for a developer tool that shares code snippets, so I can see what your output looks like. Include the ranked table.
evals.expected_output: A sample shortlist grouped by naming direction with the status-label table, flagged as illustrative, with no availability claim, no price and no pressure to register.
assertions: Groups candidates by naming direction and gives a ranked table with a status label, an RDAP URL and a source with UTC time for every checked name
Every status label is exactly `unverified`, `registered` or `not found in registry`, and any candidate marked `registered` or `not found in registry` names the lookup source and a UTC time
Says the sample's statuses are illustrative or that no live lookup produced them, rather than presenting them as current results
Never calls any name available and does not tell the user to register or buy a name immediately
Quotes no price or value estimate for any candidate and says price and renewal terms must be confirmed at a registrar
